2 OVERVIEW PHASES Resequencing describes a method for bringing system parts that are somewhere in the production process back to a defined state in order to be able to start the machine again. However, this state should not only be an initial state, but there is a modular concept that maps the respective production process and enables synchronization / start-up at all process and process-relevant points. Phases: The structuring of the production process takes place in so-called phases! The individual phases are therefore synchronization points. This phase-based concept is firmly linked to sequence programming via step chains and also to a resequencing process via step chains. Thus, in principle, resequencing also represents an automatic operating mode.

Hardware:  System control with TIA CPU1518F with integrated safety function, Periphery:	Profinet Safety Engineering:	TIA Visualization:	TIA WinCC Unified Software: Software structure The software structure of this machine is according to the GSC standard by BMW strictly derived from the AKZ. Components with their own operating mode are organized in groups. All groups and components are collected under the PLC.

"PLC" 
The “PLC” includes everything that is controlled by the central controller of this machine. In the HMI the “PLC” is also referred as “++ST000”. "GROUP" 
Components with an operating mode can be grouped to a group of operating modes. This group collects the status and enables the control of all component operating modes that belong to this group. Typically, the group is named like a station and all components of this station belong to that group. For example, a group can be called ++ST700.

"COMPONENT" 
The smallest entity of a control-technological line structure are components. Such a component can come with or without an operating mode. For example, a protective door like ++ST010+SD001 does not have an operating mode. A conveyor like ++ST700+TL001 usually has its own operating mode. Visualization The visualization that is running on each panel (HMI) is based on a basic screen that shows the whole machine. You are able to zoom in and move around. Some elements or more detailed information on an element can only be seen on specific zoom levels and below. Other elements may be only visible on a specific preselection. You can select an element by clicking on it. Once selected this element gets a blue frame around it.

General Operating modes The current operating mode is shown by the background color of the corresponding HMI element. There are the following operating modes possible: Automatic start (white) Automatic preselection (yellow) Manual mode (green) Resequencing start (blue / white) Resequencing preselection (blue) Service mode (green) General functions of the Operating modes Automatic start: All drives and units are operated, controlled or switched on and off independently by the logic of the central controller. No manual movement is possible.

The predefined normal production sequence is looped as long as new parts are provided. Automatic preselection: This operating mode is the state between “Manual” and “Automatic start”. Before you get to “Automatic start” you always need to switch “Automatic preselection” first. In this mode there will be no movement started by the logic of the central controller. Also no manual movement is possible. If a fault message of the classes “Safety Error” , “Immediate Stop” , “Stop in Home”  (delayed) or “Controlled Stop”  (delayed) are present, the operating mode will always fall back from “Automatic start” to this operating mode.

Manual mode: Interlocked manual operation of the individual system elements is possible. Operating options are available in accordance with the automatic sequence. Damage to the system and conveyed goods is prevented as far as possible. Resequencing start: All drives and units are operated, controlled or switched on and off independently by the logic of the central controller. No manual movement is possible.

The machine automatically selects the most suitable home position if possible. Subsequently the sequence to reach this home position is started once. Resequencing preselection: This operating mode is the state between “Manual” and “Resequencing start”. Before you get to “Resequencing start” you always need to switch “Resequencing preselection” first. In this mode there will be no movement started by the logic of the central controller. Also no manual movement is possible. If a fault message of the classes “Safety Error” , “Immediate Stop” , “Stop in Home”  (delayed) or “Controlled Stop”  (delayed) are present, the operating mode will always fall back from “Resequencing start” to this operating mode.

Service mode: Unlocked manual operation of all drives and units. This operating mode can only be started from “Manual”. Mechanical damage to the system is not locked! Operating modes of PLC, GROUPS and COMPONENTS The “PLC” operating mode can be selected on the top left edge. One or more “GROUP” can be selected on the preselection for operating modes in the lower left corner. All groups of this machine are then shown on the left side under the category “Groups”.

One or more “COMPONENT” with an operating mode can be selected on the preselection for operating modes in the lower left corner. All components with an operating mode of this machine are then shown on the left side under the category “FGs”. Each operating mode has an HMI element with a detail screen as shown in the picture above. To open this detail screen right click on the element of the respective operating mode. The special operating modes that are defined in the GSC-Standard are controlled by the buttons on the right.

The selected operating mode is inherited between the PLC, GROUP and COMPONENT level. So switching the operating mode with the “PLC” selected in the HMI will also switch all groups, if possible by the permissions of that panel and the current state of the line. Switching the operating mode with a “GROUP” selected in the HMI will also switch all components of that group, if possible by the permissions of that panel and the current state of the line.

In return the status of the level selected and the operating modes below is shown on the left and the middle. Under “Current mode” and “Current messages”. Fault messages The three levels of the operating modes also apply for fault messages. So the effect of a fault message on the “PLC” level will also effect all Groups and Components. And a fault message on “GROUP”-Level will also affect all “COMPONENT” in that group. Possible effects of faults include:

Safety Error  (Drop automatic start mode and drop release of manual mode) Immediate Stop  (Drop automatic start mode) Stop in Home  (Drop automatic start mode once a home position is reached) Controlled Stop  (Drop automatic start mode once all movement is stopped) Furthermore, there are the following fault messages, that have no effect to the operating mode, but may have an indirect effect: Error without Stop

Each button can be selected any time but will be active only when the sequence has reached the selected constellation. When any of the four buttons is active the sequence is halted until the active button is deselected again. So the production will stop even though the whole line remains in the “Automatic start” operating mode.

Stop before process: This button will stop the station before the process starts. After an unfinished part has entered the station and is prepared for the process. Stop after process: This button will stop the station after finishing the process of the current part. The finished part will remain in the position required for the process. The robot repeats the process until the count provided in the HMI for “Input MFU2 TF1 Cycle Count” is reached. Go inside to remove the processed coupons for inspection.
